name: High-yield credit spread
why: Credit usually cracks before equities. Spreads were near 3-4% in calm years, 5-6% in the 2015-16 and 2022 scares, and 8% or more in recessions.

name: Yield curve, 10 years minus 2 years
why: An inverted curve has preceded every US recession since the 1970s, with a lag of 6 to 24 months.

name: 10-year Treasury yield
why: Long-duration growth stocks and AI build-out financing are the most exposed to higher discount rates. Feeds the bonds bet (BOND forecasts).

name: Inflation expectations, 5 years from 5 years ahead
why: Sticky inflation with rising rates is the scenario none of the current bets hedges.

name: Brent crude
why: An oil shock feeds inflation and squeezes consumers and airlines. Feeds the airlines bet.

name: Sahm rule, real time
why: 0.5 is the rule's recession signal; 0.3 is an early warning.

name: Chicago Fed financial conditions
why: Zero is average conditions; positive is tighter than average.

name: VIX
why: Implied equity volatility; above 30 has marked forced selling.

name: Margin debt, change on a year earlier
why: Leverage built fast late in 1999-2000, 2007 and 2021. FINRA publishes debit balances in customers' securities margin accounts monthly.
how: Monthly. FINRA margin statistics (debit balances in customers' securities margin accounts); record the change on the same month a year earlier, in percent.

name: AI financing stress, CoreWeave 2031 bond yield
why: Theme risk, not part of the regime. Neocloud borrowing costs show how hard it is to finance the AI build-out. Feeds the AI build-out delay bet.
how: Weekly. Yield to worst on CoreWeave's 2031 senior notes from a primary or reputable market source (FINRA TRACE, issuer filings, or financial press quoting a price).
